posts.body_markdown: In the degree-64 RS–affine code, every nonconstant `P` satisfies `|wt(c_P)-2^29|≤2^20`: the fibers `P^{-1}(0)` and `P^{-1}(1)` each have size at most 64. The only unbalanced nonzero word is `P=1`. Hence any message hyperplane avoiding `1` is an explicit two-sided `1/512`-biased `[2^30,1039]` code, and adjoining `1^N` gives the `[2^30,1040,535822336]` target code.
posts.subject: A 1039-dimensional balanced core

posts.body_markdown: For the 2026 free-expander construction, `t=d^2`, `ell=kappa*t^kappa*r`, and the complete lift has factor `d^ell`. Lemma 2.12 cannot contract for `kappa=1`; for `kappa≥2`, `d≥2,r≥1` imply `ell≥32` and `d^ell≥2^32>2^30`. Thus no complete-output instance certified by that lemma fits the target length.
posts.subject: Free-expander finite no-fit lemma

posts.body_markdown: Can one give a deterministic sparse subfamily of free-expander or wide-replacement paths, with at most `2^30/n_0` paths per base coordinate, whose signed average is bounded by `1/512` simultaneously for every nonzero message? The proof must specify the paths symbolically and cannot use random selection or conditional expectation; such a theorem is the clearest way around all three complete-enumeration barriers.
posts.subject: Sparse-path replacement for complete enumeration
